extraction_notes: P-channel polarity is retained in signed electrical table values and in curve points where the source plot uses VDS, VGS, or ID; resistance and capacitance remain positive physical quantities.

Output, transfer, and capacitance curves were digitized directly from p. 3 Figs. 1, 2, and 3 at selected visible axis positions without interpolation between unobserved observations. The source plots display p-channel magnitudes (-ID and negative gate labels); curve points here retain the corresponding signs and are converted to SI units.

The static table publishes RDS(on) typical values of 0.075 ohm at VGS = -10 V, ID = -1.9 A and 0.115 ohm at VGS = -4.5 V, ID = -1.4 A; corresponding MAX values are 0.19 ohm and 0.33 ohm. The represented rdson_points use the published typical values.
The static table publishes IDSS MAX -1 uA at VDS = -30 V, VGS = 0 V and IGSS MAX +/-100 nA at VGS = +/-20 V, VDS = 0 V; the schema has no dedicated leakage fields.

The dynamic and switching tables publish Qg typical 4 nC (MAX 8 nC) and 2 nC (MAX 4 nC) under separate conditions, Qgs typical 0.6 nC, Qgd typical 1 nC, Qrr typical 4 nC, and trr typical 24.5 ns at IF = -3 A and di/dt = 100 A/us; the schema has no dedicated gate-charge or reverse-recovery fields.
The switching table publishes Rg min 1.7 ohm, typical 8.5 ohm, and MAX 17 ohm at f = 1 MHz; the schema has no dedicated gate-resistance field.

The maximum ratings table publishes VDS = -30 V, VGS = +/-20 V, ID = -1.9 A, IS = -0.83 A, PD = 0.35 W, RthetaJA = 357 K/W, and TJ/TSTG = -55 to +150 degC. The schema has no dedicated maximum-rating or thermal-resistance fields.

Figure 3 is labelled Capacitance Characteristics in the supplied PDF and shows Ciss, Coss, and Crss versus VDS at TJ = 25 degC; the figure does not specify VGS or frequency, while the tabulated capacitances are specified at VDS = -15 V, VGS = 0 V, and f = 1 MHz.
